newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Thailand plans land reclamation for LNG imports.
newsitem.headline: Thailand plans land reclamation for LNG imports.

text.p: Thailand plans to start land reclamation in April as part of work to build a three-million tonnes-per-year terminal to receive imports of liquefied natural gas (LNG), a senior official of Thai LNG Power Corp Ltd (TLPC) said on Monday.

"The preparation work has been carried exactly on schedule," Dulapol Anussorn-Nitisara, vice president of TLPC, told a gas conference in Singapore. A copy of his remarks was made available to Reuters.
"TLPC already got approval from the National Environmental Board to reclaim the land and constructing the LNG receiving terminal," in Rayong province, he said.
"It is expected that the actual reclamation will start in April 1997 and the construction of the terminal will be around mid of year 1999," he added.
The initial budget for vaporisers, two storage tanks and a jetty is around U.S.$700 million, Dulapol said.
He said current natural gas demand in Thailand was 1,500 million cubic feet per day but was estimated to double by 2001, reflecting the expansion of the economy.
Thailand's natural gas reserves, of around 6.2 trillion cubic feet, are expected to be depleted by 2008.
Dulapol said state-oil firm Petroleum Authority of Thailand (PTT) expected imports of natural gas to reach 2,000 million cubic feet per day by 2011, with power generation the major consumer.
